audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is absent from both layers: empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields on its target. Nothing anywhere says it, and the entry actively advises the reader in the opposite direction — whys[6] tells you your "Repudiation shield compound[s] in long fights" and report[8] recommends Sterak's Gage as a core item.
audit.why: Riot's Ruthless Predator text: "If Renekton has more than 50 Fury, he slashes his target three times, destroying damage shields on the target, dealing high physical damage, and stunning them for 1.5 seconds." Ambessa's only defensive layer is Repudiation, a shield. So above 50 Fury Renekton removes her defensive ability and her recommended second item in one cast, and doubles the stun from 0.75s to 1.5s at the same time. Every trade rule in the entry is built on a shield that will not be there.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[0], wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], whys[6], breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[0], report[5] and report[8]; Sterak's Gage removed from the core build with the reason attached; the Fury threshold given as the tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings credit Public Execution with effects it does not have: spikes[2] says "your R passive armor-pen and heal-on-damage", mid says "the R passive armor-pen plus heal-on-ability-damage", and whys[4] says "your R passive armor-pen finishes the all-in".
audit.why: Riot's Public Execution text is "blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival. She then slams the enemy into the ground where they take damage and are stunned." There is no armour penetration and no healing in it, and Ambessa has no passive that grants either — Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund. This is a fabricated stat being used as the reason the level-6 all-in works, which means the reader commits on maths that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the reason the all-in actually works: suppression is the one form of lockdown Renekton's Fury cannot buy his way out of, and it lands while Slice and Dice is still his only exit.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why says "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade", and the spike list gives no cooldown numbers at all, so "his cooldowns are short, yours are long" is asserted without a single figure.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants no shield. And the cooldown asymmetry the entry keeps gesturing at is real and quantifiable: Ruthless Predator goes 16s to 8s across its ranks while Ambessa's Lacerate only goes 13s to 9s and Repudiation 18s to 14s, so by levels 4-5 his stun is up for most waves and her answer is not. Cull the Meek is a flat 7s at every rank.
audit.corrected: Passive shield claim removed; real numbers written into spikes[2], spikes[3], breakdown.cooldowns and the do/don't descriptions.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagrees with its own prose at five of seven stages. It opens "Skill" while whys[0] says his W-stun and double strike "own level 1 ... farm, don't fight"; it gives Renekton level 3 while whys[2] says "neither wins on demand"; it gives Ambessa levels 4-5 while whys[3] says "concede the window and farm to six"; and it gives Renekton both item stages while whys[5] and whys[6] say to force fights and that Ambessa's scaling edges the lane.
audit.why: At 49.08% over 1202 games this is close to a true coinflip, but the shape is not flat — Renekton is an early-game bully whose kit falls off, and the packet levelChart (Renekton, Renekton, Skill, Renekton, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa) matches the prose exactly. The chart as written tells the reader to fight in the two windows the text tells them to concede.
audit.corrected: Not changed. Every required flip on this matchup crosses the length band — "Skill" is 5 characters and "Renekton" is 8, "Ambessa" is 7 — so the applier would reject all of them. Documented in notes for the user to apply by hand.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] recommends Sterak's Gage as the second core item. Anti-heal is mentioned but with no reason and no timing.
audit.why: Sterak's Gage is a shield, and above 50 Fury Renekton's W destroys damage shields on the target — the item's defining effect is the one thing he deletes on demand. Separately, Cull the Meek heals on a flat 7s cooldown at every rank and heals more above 50 Fury, so the anti-heal recommendation is right but needs the number to be actionable.
audit.corrected: Sterak's removed from core with the shield-strip reason; anti-heal tied to Cull the Meek's 7s cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/renekton.json (Q cd 7 flat, heal; W destroys damage shields)

TWO PACKET FALSE POSITIVES on this matchup: suspectNames flags "His Ruthless Predator" (early) and "Then Public Execution" (mid). Both ability names are spelled correctly; the edit distance comes from the leading word. No name error exists in this entry.

THE REAL ERROR the scanner could not see is the reverse: correct names, invented effects. "R passive armor-pen and heal-on-damage" appears three times as the stated reason the level-6 all-in works. Public Execution has neither. Worth noting that the same phrasing shows up in the Ambessa vs Aatrox entry ("r-pen plus the crash-down burst"), so this is probably a champion-wide fabrication rather than one bad string — a grep for "armor-pen" and "heal-on" across champ-data/content/ambessa.js and champ-data/ambessa.full.js would be worth running.
